JavaScript.question: Which of these is NOT a JavaScript primitive type?
JavaScript.explanation: JavaScript has seven primitive types: string, number, boolean, null, undefined, symbol and bigint. `object` is a reference type, so it is not a primitive.

JavaScript.question: What does the strict equality operator === compare?
JavaScript.explanation: === is strict equality: it compares both the value and the type, so `1 === "1"` is false. The loose == operator converts types before comparing.

JavaScript.question: Which array method adds an item to the END of an array?
JavaScript.explanation: push() adds an item to the end of an array. shift() removes from the front, unshift() adds to the front, and pop() removes from the end.

JavaScript.question: What does typeof null return?
JavaScript.explanation: A well-known quirk of the language: typeof null returns "object". It dates back to the original implementation and was kept for backwards compatibility, even though null is a primitive.

JavaScript.question: Which function converts a string into a whole number?
JavaScript.explanation: parseInt() reads a string and returns a whole number. toString() converts a value to a string, Number.isNaN() checks whether a value is NaN, and join() joins array elements into a string.

React.question: Which hook is used to store local state in a component?
React.explanation: useState returns the current state value and a setter to update it. useEffect runs side effects, useMemo memoises a computed value, and useRef holds a mutable reference.

React.question: In React, what are props?
options: Data passed from a parent to a child component
CSS classes applied to a component
Global variables shared by every component
React.explanation: Props are read-only inputs passed from a parent component to a child. They are not state, and a child must never mutate them directly.

React.question: Which hook runs side effects after render?
React.explanation: useEffect runs side effects after render — data fetching, subscriptions or manual DOM updates. useState holds state, useContext reads context, and useReducer handles complex state logic.

React.question: What should every item in a rendered list have?
React.explanation: A unique key lets React tell which list items changed, were added or were removed, so it can update the DOM efficiently and correctly.

React.question: Which array method is commonly used to render a list in JSX?
React.explanation: map() transforms each item into a JSX element and returns the array to render. filter(), reduce() and sort() do not return an array of JSX elements for rendering.

HTML & CSS.question: Which HTML tag creates a hyperlink?
HTML & CSS.explanation: The <a> tag with an href attribute creates a clickable hyperlink. <link> is used to link external resources such as stylesheets, not to make links on the page.

HTML & CSS.question: Which CSS property changes the colour of text?
HTML & CSS.explanation: The `color` property sets the colour of text. `background` sets the background, `font-weight` sets how bold the text is, and `fill` colours SVG shapes.

HTML & CSS.question: Which display value turns an element into a flex container?
HTML & CSS.explanation: display: flex turns an element into a flex container, which makes its direct children flex items that can be aligned and spaced with flexbox properties.

HTML & CSS.question: Which CSS unit is relative to the ROOT font size?
HTML & CSS.explanation: rem is relative to the root (<html>) font size, which makes it predictable for scaling. em is relative to the element's own font size, px is an absolute unit, and vh is relative to viewport height.

HTML & CSS.question: Which property adds space INSIDE an element's border?
HTML & CSS.explanation: padding adds space inside an element, between its content and its border. margin adds space outside the border, separating the element from its neighbours.
